changelog: v350: one couple, one alias, one label. WHERE THEY WERE SEEN: the owner's own vault, 2026-09-24, all three in the same ordinary sweep — `entity-roster --ensure-introduced`, `bind-episodes --apply`, `publish` — and the roster introduction is what armed all three. DEFECT 1, A COUPLE IS TWO PEOPLE, NOT ONE RELATIONSHIP WORD. `node:b8681112f7eed9342e7e4d56` "Wedding reception in mother-in-law's backyard" — the OWNER's reception, subject `self`, his own anniversary 2007-01-11 — was folded into `node:536bdbed274f9512cc6c0378` at 1976-06-25, his PARENTS' wedding, together with `claim:34c92ccbf218e122a181ca5f` ("Mom married dad at 21") and `claim:e331cefd22c5a2c5670d861b` ("Parents' wedding date"), and the merged node published `subject_refs: ["Author's parents", "person/desiree-taylor", "self"]` and `conflict_state: contradicted`. It surfaced as a contradiction card, so v340's semantics held; the merge was still wrong. AND IT WAS NOT v345's COUPLE KEY THAT TOOK IT. The introduction filed `mother` as a bare alias of `person/desiree-taylor`; `episode_containers.resolve_entities` matches a contiguous TOKEN RUN; `mother-in-law` tokenizes to `(mother, in, law)`. So the word inside the compound resolved to the owner's MOTHER, the reception's person tokens became `{desiree, taylor}`, and `R2b`'s per-PERSON milestone bucket — `married:desiree` — read the reception and the age telling as two tellings of one marriage, with the age telling supplying no date of its own to contradict. THE RULE (`episode_binder.A_COUPLE_IS_TWO_PEOPLE`), two legs and one seat each. (1) A COMPOUND RELATIONSHIP WORD IS NEVER THE SIMPLE WORD INSIDE IT (`identity_resolution.A_COMPOUND_RELATION_IS_NEVER_THE_WORD_INSIDE_IT`, `_not_a_simple_relation` — v347's `_NOT_A_POSSESSOR` in the other direction): a matched run that IS one relationship word is refused when the words around it make it a different relationship — an in-law suffix behind it, read through the ONE `IN_LAW_RE` (moved from `axis_membership` to `identity_resolution`, beside the `RELATIONSHIP_MENTION_WORDS` vocabulary it is a reading of, and re-exported under its old name so `roster_relations` still finds it: one regex, not two that agree today), or a `COMPOUND_RELATION_PREFIXES` word in front of it (step, grand, great, half, god, foster, adoptive, ex, former, late). It sits in `resolve_entities`, the seat that resolved the wrong person, so every rung that reads a roster match is fixed once rather than `R2b` alone. A LONGER key is the compound itself and still matches — a roster that knows a mother-in-law BY THAT PHRASE resolves her by it — and a bare "mother" still resolves, which is what an introduction is FOR. (2) A COUPLE KEY IS READ FROM THE TELLING'S OWN SUBJECTS (`identity_resolution.couple_key`, now handed the new `episode_binder.TellingView.subject_mentions` rather than the tokenized person set). The subjects are what a telling is ABOUT; a word in a backyard is not. The OWNER's own subject names the OWNER's couple — `self`, `me`, `narrator` (`OWNER_SUBJECT_MENTIONS`) and the first-person plural `we`/`our`/`us` (`OWNER_COUPLE_SUBJECT_WORDS`, scoped to this reading alone because "we" names somebody besides the owner as well as the owner) — so a telling of "our wedding" belongs to his couple and can never reach his parents'. v345's vocabulary is unchanged and every one of its pinned couple_key answers still holds; under a resolved roster the subject-side reading RESTORES v345's own pair, because the introduction had already turned the age telling's person tokens into `{desiree, taylor}` and the people-side key had quietly stopped finding the couple it was written for. DEFECT 2, AN IDENTITY RE-KEY PUBLISHES AN ALIAS — v346 documented the seam and this closes it, as the FIFTH way a node id moves (v342 closed three, all acts of the identity layer; v345 added the landmark redraw; this one is the RESOLVER naming a subject nobody had named before). A node id is derived from its subject and `_subject_handle` reads "the resolved ref when identity landed, the raw mention when it did not", so the moment the introduction made "Dad graduated" resolve to `person/james-taylor` the node moved — `node:1bdbc9ecc7305d5a90c6e4a4` (1987) became `node:2156ca1018344c8248882c44` (1987) for the identical claim `claim:cd8e993b6bf95a5f4c80c862` — and NO `node_aliases` redirect was published, so the v340/v342 audit reported a lost placement and every card, session and URL still naming the old id broke. `temporal_timeline._identity_rekeys` is the ONE derivation of the map and `_group_claims` and `_identity_rekey_aliases` are its two readers: the former id is ARITHMETIC over the mention the claim still carries — resolution is data about a claim and never an edit of one — so nothing is read off the previous publication and the drawing stays a function of the receipts. Both of v342's dispositions apply unchanged, because they are the two things that can be true of a key that moved: a key nothing publishes any more is published as `old -> new` and reported `identity_subject_rekeyed`, and a key some claim STILL publishes is not redirected — that claim is CARRIED onto the new id instead. The carry is what the duplicate undated "Mom babysat Kodi and Acey Nixon" node of the v346/v347 reports needed: the resolver reading of that stay froze the old id into its own `event_ref`, so when the derived key moved the fold drew one fact twice — once dated 1982-08/1986-06 at `node:0907f1e77149ddc33da60957`, once undated at `node:ad829b67cd14b859094b1c5d`, the undated copy carrying a fresh "when?" card the node beside it answers. A claim follows the node it folds under, whichever act moved that node. Three refusals, all quiet and all v345's or v342's own: a claim carrying its own `event_ref` never moved (its id was never derived from a subject), a former id two claims disagree about the destination of is dropped whole, and a map that would be a CHAIN drops both ends. DEFECT 3, A CARD NEVER SHOWS A NODE ID AS ITS LABEL — v343's "a card is asked only when a person could answer it", reaching the one rung that had escaped it. `question_planner` minted `missing_anchor` items whose whole `prompt_intent` was "When was node:0809d05e26d18f128fd83126?" with `subject_ref: anchor:node 0809d05e26d18f128fd83126` — 28 `missing_anchor` cards on the hosted head, 22 of them carrying an id, and 13 of which 10 after the sweep — because a cross-dating anchor may be a NODE REF and the anchor composer asked about whatever text it was handed. TWO SEATS (`temporal_timeline.A_CARD_NEVER_SHOWS_A_NODE_ID_AS_ITS_LABEL`), and the second is the one that cannot fall behind. The RUNG mints nothing for a handle that names an internal id (`conversation_lints.names_an_internal_id`), before the roster is even asked about it, and reports `anchor_without_a_human_label` with the nodes that were waiting — which is the only place this was ever visible, and dropping the card loses nothing because every one of those nodes already carries a card of its own (48 of 48 on the head this was measured on). And the LINT refuses any composed sentence carrying one (a fifth refusal in `lint_question`, the backstop every composer already routes through), so no template in any composer can emit an id even by accident. The shape is DERIVED from the minter — `temporal_claims.ID_RE`'s `<prefix>:<digest>`, so `node:`, `claim:`, `work:`, `episode:`, `edge:`, `membership:` and whatever prefix comes next are all covered — rather than from a hand list of prefixes, which is v349's own lesson applied: a centralized definition whose INPUTS are a hand list is not centralized. The genuine anchors are kept ("When was 701 North Williams foreclosure?", "When was Dad's death?") and ONE grammar rule joins them rather than a hand list: a phrase that LEADS with a verb is a bare predicate whatever its length (`_leads_with_a_verb`, `_is_gerund_phrase`'s mirror, sharing its `_ING_EVENT_NOUNS` vocabulary so "wedding reception" stays the noun phrase it is), replacing a word COUNT that made "moved in with dad" a clause and "left Kristen" not one — so "When was left Kristen?" becomes "You mentioned left Kristen — when was that?", the same sentence the four-word phrase beside it already got. `CALCULATION_RULE_VERSION` MOVES to `timeline-rules:17`: nodes, aliases AND cards all change for a vault nobody edited, and the goldens and the nine pinned assertions move with it as v343-v347's did. MEASURED on a scratch clone of the owner's vault (`/private/tmp/lifehug-rig-v350`, head `cf3d996a`; the original was never written to), repaired first with v349's own `landmark-reinstate --domain residences --since 2026-09-24T19:17:00Z --apply` (29 supersessions reinstated, 89 claims restored, 33 residences entries drawn) and then swept: `entity-roster --ensure-introduced` filed 4 rows, `bind-episodes --apply` filed 7 envelopes and 338 proposals, `publish` went generation 169 -> 170. The wedding reception stays `node:b8681112f7eed9342e7e4d56` at 2007-01-11, subject `self`, `conflict_state: none`, before and after the sweep; his parents' wedding stays its own node at 1976-06-25. NINE node ids moved across the sweep and all nine carry an alias (`node_aliases` 1020 -> 1029, five of them `identity_subject_rekeyed`). The lost-placement audit is EMPTY in all three legs — nothing lost, nothing moved to an incompatible date, and no node drawn at an id `node_aliases` has redirected. ZERO of the 57 open cards carry `node:` in their prompt; the cards by kind are contradiction 11, identity_uncertain 1, missing_anchor 5, place_ambiguous 3, precision_gap 37, and the five anchor cards read "When was 701 North Williams foreclosure?", "When was Dad's death?", "You mentioned earning Eagle Scout in Arizona — when was that?", "You mentioned moved in with dad — when was that?" and "You mentioned left Kristen — when was that?". Nineteen anchor handles were refused as `anchor_without_a_human_label`. On a SEPARATE copy of the already-swept vault the three readings take open cards 76 -> 65, `missing_anchor` 13 -> 3, cards carrying an id 10 -> 0, and the "Mom babysat" nodes 4 -> 3 with the 1982-08/1986-06 date carried onto the survivor and the old id redirected. GUARDS: `tests/test_v350_one_couple_one_alias_one_label.py` (59 tests, 76 subtests) — three sections, each of the owner's real shapes as a fixture on a synthetic vault. The reception beside the parents' wedding and the age telling, proved two nodes at their own dates with no rung binding them, and the defect REPRODUCED by monkeypatching each leg out in turn so the two are proved independent; every compound spelling a person writes refused and every bare relationship word still resolving; a roster that knows a mother-in-law by that phrase still resolving her; v345's whole couple_key vocabulary re-asserted; the graduation re-key with its alias, its finding, its claim set and its date; the babysat duplicate proved to become one dated node with the old id redirected and no card; the map's three refusals; the alias refused when the drawing still publishes the key and when the target is not drawn; the v340/v342 placement audit over the whole re-key with lost, moved and drawn-at-an-alias all empty, and the audit proved to SEE the defect when the alias is withheld; `AN_ALIAS_NEVER_NAMES_A_NODE_THE_DRAWING_PUBLISHES` as a one-line invariant over the release that adds a fourth source of aliases; determinism over reversed input order; the lint refusing an id of every prefix and leaving ordinary sentences alone; the derived shape proved not to be a prefix list; the rung minting nothing and reporting the nodes that were waiting, each of which still has a card; and no card in ANY whole-vault derivation in the file carrying an id. ONE PIN LOOSENED ON THE WAY: `tests/test_v349_*`'s `test_the_release_is_v349` asserted `version == 349`, which makes every later bump fail a test about a landmark rule; it now asserts the release it guards has SHIPPED (`>= 349`), which is what it was for. Full local suite: 6703 tests, 6698 passed, 1 failed (the known macOS-only `test_file_answer_outer_queue_leaves_no_plaintext_temp`), 4 skipped, and the checkout clean afterwards. Ruff parity held exactly: `identity_resolution.py`, `episode_containers.py`, `episode_binder.py`, `temporal_timeline.py`, `conversation_lints.py` and `axis_membership.py` match their v349 finding sets message for message, 80 findings to 80, with nothing new on either side.
